title: GH#18998: fix review-followup scanner to skip empty bot reviews
body:
## Summary

Fixes two related issues that create noise in the review-followup pipeline:

1. **Empty-review guard** (`quality-feedback-findings-lib.sh`): the scanner fires on PRs where bots post "no feedback" summaries with zero actionable inline comments, creating false-positive quality-debt issues (incident: GH#18834).

2. **raw-sandbox-output over-suppression** (`pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh`): a triage worker's valid `## Review: Decline` header was suppressed as `raw-sandbox-output` because surrounding log lines confused the sed extraction, preventing the closing comment from being posted.

## Changes

### Fix 1 — PR-level empty-review guard in `_scan_single_pr`

Adds a check AFTER computing `inline_counts_json`: if total inline comment count across all reviewers is 0 **and** every review body matches a negative-finding regex (`no feedback|no review comments|no issues found|lgtm|looks good to me|nothing to flag|...`), return `[]` immediately with a `skip: empty-review PR#N` log line.

- Bypassed when `--include-positive` is set (debugging mode)
- Belt-and-suspenders: the existing per-reviewer `summary_only` filter still runs; this guard catches the case where `state=APPROVED` (not `COMMENTED`) slips through

### Fix 2 — Tighten `raw-sandbox-output` classification

Before classifying as `raw-sandbox-output` (no `## Review` header + infra markers), check if the first non-empty line of `review_text` is `^## Review:`. If it is, re-extract from that line and post (with the normal post-extraction infra check). This handles encoding quirks (CRLF, BOM, raw-mode output) that prevent the existing sed pattern from matching.

## Testing

- 3 new unit tests in `test-quality-feedback-main-verification.sh`:
  - Gemini APPROVED `"no feedback"` + 0 inline comments → 0 findings (GH#18834 regression)
  - Multiple bots all negative + 0 inline → 0 findings
  - Negative top-level summary + inline comments → guard does **not** fire (no over-suppression)
- All 3 pass; only pre-existing `transient API error` test still fails (unrelated, pre-dated this PR)
- ShellCheck: zero violations on all 3 modified files

Resolves #18998

title: t2099: auto-apply 'good first issue' label to tier:simple issues

## Summary

- Extend `_apply_tier_label_replace` in `issue-sync-helper.sh` so `tier:simple` issues automatically also get GitHub's standard `good first issue` label.
- Only applied on `tier:simple`; never auto-removed on escalation (defers to `_is_protected_label` policy).

## Why

`tier:simple` issues are, by definition, prescriptive single-file pattern-follows with verbatim code blocks — the exact shape of a community-friendly first contribution. We already produce this pool mechanically; we just were not labelling it for external discovery. Surfacing via GitHub's standard `good first issue` label exposes them to the built-in community filter and third-party discovery sites (goodfirstissue.dev, up-for-grabs, code-triage).

## Design

- **Only ADD, never auto-remove.** `good first issue` is already in `_is_protected_label` and may reflect deliberate human intent. Removing it on escalation would fight maintainer signal.
- **Ensure-then-add.** Uses the existing `gh_create_label` helper (`--force`, idempotent) so repos that don't yet have the label get it created at first application.
- **Gated on the exact tier string.** `[[ "$new_tier" == "tier:simple" ]]` — standard/thinking escalations are unaffected.

## Summary

- `full-loop-helper.sh start` now **automatically claims the linked issue** for interactive sessions, closing the race window where the pulse could dispatch a duplicate worker
- `interactive-session-helper.sh claim` now **posts a claim comment** on the issue for audit trail visibility
- `full-loop.md` Step 0 documents the structural enforcement

### The problem

When an interactive session runs `/full-loop` on an issue, the claim was prompt-only — the AI had to remember to call `interactive-session-helper.sh claim`. In the GH#18775 session, it was missed. The pulse could have dispatched a duplicate worker during the ~30 minute window between "start working" and "PR created".

### The fix

Three enforcement layers:

| Layer | File | What |

title: t2111: fix(issue-sync): ratchet rule in _apply_tier_label_replace — preserve cascade-escalated tier labels
body:
## Summary

`escalate_issue_tier()` in `worker-lifecycle-common.sh` writes escalated tier labels directly to GitHub but leaves the brief file unchanged. The scheduled `issue-sync` enrichment pass then reads the brief and reverts the escalation via `_apply_tier_label_replace`, producing a `tier:standard → tier:thinking → tier:standard` flip-flop visible on GH#19038 label event history (00:38:49 escalate, 00:44:15/16 revert, 01:20 dispatch at `tier:standard` again → same failure).

Fix: add a max-rank **ratchet** to `_apply_tier_label_replace`. Compute the max rank among existing `tier:*` labels using `thinking(2) > standard(1) > simple(0)`. If the existing max outranks the incoming tier, no-op with an info log. Otherwise proceed with the existing replace-all logic. Semantic: brief is a floor, cascade is a ceiling, ceiling wins.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh`
  - Added `_tier_rank` helper (case-statement, O(1)) with a cross-reference comment pointing at the canonical `ISSUE_TIER_LABEL_RANK` in `shared-constants.sh`.
  - Added a ratchet guard inside `_apply_tier_label_replace` that iterates the currently-applied `tier:*` labels, computes the max rank, and returns early with `print_info` when the existing max exceeds the incoming rank.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tier-label-ratchet.sh` (new, 23 tests)
  - 6 `_tier_rank` unit tests (simple/standard/thinking/empty/unknown/non-tier).
  - 7 ratchet-preservation tests including the exact #19038 flip-flop case (`existing=tier:thinking, incoming=tier:standard → no-op`) and multi-tier collisions.
  - 7 pre-existing-behaviour regression tests (upgrades, bootstrap, idempotent equal) that must not regress.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: **Low** — local shell helper covered by a dedicated test harness; no network, no filesystem side effects outside stubbed `gh`. Self-assessed.

Verification:

```text
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tier-label-ratchet.sh         → 23/23 pass
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tier-label-dedup.sh           → 13/13 pass (regression)
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-tier-extraction.sh → 8/8 pass  (regression — includes its own _apply_tier_label_replace assertions, unchanged semantics)
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-label-invariants.sh           → 19/19 pass (regression — reconciler uses same thinking > standard > simple ordering)
shellcheck .agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh               → exit 0 (pre-existing SC1091/SC2016 info-level only)
```

End-to-end proof: patched function run against a stubbed `tier:thinking` issue with a `tier:standard` brief produces zero `gh issue edit` API calls — the trace file is empty, ratchet holds.

## Design Decisions

- **Local `_tier_rank` vs indexing `ISSUE_TIER_LABEL_RANK` from shared-constants:** chose local. The shared array orders `thinking=0` (rank order as position), which would invert the numeric comparison needed here, and a case statement is O(1) without array iteration. Added a comment cross-reference so the relationship is explicit.
- **Ratchet vs write-back to brief:** chose ratchet. Writing escalated tiers back to the brief file would require a commit-per-escalation path, race with concurrent edits, and add cross-file coordination. The ratchet is local to one function, deterministic, and matches the existing max-tier-wins semantics already implemented by `_resolve_worker_tier` (pulse-dispatch-core.sh) and `_first_tier_in_rank_order` (pulse-issue-reconcile.sh).
- **Multi-tier collision handling:** when the issue somehow has both e.g. `tier:simple` and `tier:thinking` AND the incoming is `tier:standard`, the ratchet no-ops entirely (max rank 2 > incoming 1). This is a rare degenerate state; the pulse-issue-reconcile.sh invariant reconciler separately ensures only one tier label per issue, so the collision is transient and the ratchet's "preserve max" behaviour matches the reconciler's own pick.

## Evidence of the Bug

`#19038` label event timeline (via `gh api events`):

```text
00:44:15  github-actions[bot]   -tier:thinking
00:44:16  github-actions[bot]   +tier:standard                   (_apply_tier_label_replace reverts)
01:20:20  pulse dispatches tier:standard again → same worker_failed
```

title: GH#19044: fix(pulse): resolve FD exhaustion causing merge pass cycles to never complete

## Summary

## Root cause

The launchd plist for the supervisor pulse inherited the macOS default soft FD limit of 256. The pulse sources ~20 modules and spawns gh/jq/git subprocesses across multiple repos per cycle — 256 FDs is structurally insufficient. Additionally, `_simplification_state_refresh()` used process substitution (`< <(jq ...)`) inside a per-file while loop, which leaks FDs in bash 3.2 (the `/bin/bash` version on macOS).

**Effect**: FD exhaustion (`cannot duplicate fd: Too many open files`) caused stages to fail silently, the progress watchdog then killed the pulse before `deterministic_merge_pass` could run, leaving worker PRs unmerged.

## Changes

1. **pulse-wrapper.sh**: Added `ulimit -n 4096` at startup (before sourcing modules) to raise the soft FD limit from 256 to 4096. Added a regression guard that warns if the limit is below 1024.

2. **pulse-simplification-state.sh**: Replaced process substitution (`< <(jq ...)`) with command substitution + here-string (`$(...) <<<`) in `_simplification_state_refresh()` and `_simplification_state_backfill_closed()` to eliminate FD leaks in bash 3.2.

3. **setup-modules/schedulers.sh**: Added `SoftResourceLimits.NumberOfFiles=4096` to the launchd plist generation as defence-in-depth.

title: t2116: fix(pulse-merge): update-branch + NMR skip before CONFLICTING-close
body:
Resolves #19106

## Root cause

Over the last 48h of `marcusquinn/aidevops`, **10 of 17 closed-unmerged PRs (~59%) were auto-closed by `pulse-merge.sh`** with `merge conflicts with the base branch` — despite the workers having solved the tasks correctly (all CI green, all tests passing). They sat waiting for a merge cycle while `main` advanced (e.g. ratchet PRs on `complexity-thresholds.conf`, sibling simplifications on `brief/templates.md`), their `mergeable` field flipped to `CONFLICTING`, and `_close_conflicting_pr` immediately closed them. Re-dispatch from scratch → same race → same close → perpetual loop on contended files.

Concrete cases in that window: #19094, #19083, #18988, #18921, #18818, #18944, #18946, #19018.

## Two pathologies fixed

### 1. Skip CONFLICTING-close for `needs-maintainer-review` PRs

`_process_single_ready_pr` previously checked `mergeable=CONFLICTING` at line 925 **before** the maintainer gate at line 947. A PR parked legitimately waiting for maintainer approval was killed the moment `main` advanced — punishing review latency by discarding worker effort. PR #18988 (created 19:25, closed 20:29 after ~1h wait) and #19083 both hit this exactly.

Now: if the linked issue carries `needs-maintainer-review`, the CONFLICTING-close path is skipped entirely and a one-time rebase nudge is posted (same shape as the existing `origin:interactive` skip).

### 2. Attempt `gh pr update-branch` before closing

Most observed conflicts are purely base-branch advancement on an adjacent file — GitHub's server-side merger can fast-forward `main` into the branch for free. When that succeeds, `mergeable` is re-fetched and the PR continues through the normal merge path in the **same cycle**. Only true semantic conflicts (update-branch returns non-zero) fall through to the close path.

## Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` — new `_attempt_pr_update_branch` helper and reworked CONFLICTING handling in `_process_single_ready_pr`. ~90 lines added, zero lines removed from existing close logic (defensive: the close path is still there for true conflicts).
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-update-branch.sh` — 5 new tests covering update-branch success/failure, log-tag audit, NMR guard structural verification, and the mergeable-refetch requirement.

## Verification

- All 6 pulse-merge test suites pass: 45 tests total, 0 failures.
- `shellcheck`: zero violations on both modified/added files.
- `bash -n`: syntax clean.

## Follow-ups (separate issues, not blocking this PR)

- Dispatch throttle on overlapping file footprints — prevent parallel CONFLICTING cascades at the source.
- Carry forward the closed PR's diff as worker guidance on the linked issue so the re-dispatched worker starts from work-in-progress rather than from scratch.

title: t2118: carry forward closed-CONFLICTING PR diff to linked issue
body:
## Summary

When `_close_conflicting_pr` closes a worker PR via the "work NOT on main" path, the solved diff was silently discarded. The next worker would re-derive the same solution, hit the same conflict, and the loop would repeat — burning tokens on redundant work.

This PR breaks that loop by carrying the PR diff forward to the linked issue body, giving the next worker a concrete starting point.

## Changes

- **`_carry_forward_pr_diff()` helper** added to `pulse-merge.sh` (new function after `_close_conflicting_pr`):
  - Fetches `gh pr diff` for the closed PR
  - Size-caps at 20KB with truncation note
  - Appends under `## Prior worker attempt (PR #NNN, closed CONFLICTING)` in a `<details>` block
  - Idempotency guard: `<!-- t2118:prior-worker-diff:PR<N> -->` marker prevents duplicate appends
  - Fail-open: any gh API failure is logged and the close still proceeds

- **`_close_conflicting_pr`** updated: in the "work NOT on main" else-branch, extract the linked issue and call `_carry_forward_pr_diff` before the `gh pr close` call

- **Regression test** `test-pulse-merge-carry-forward-diff.sh` (5 assertions):
  1. Happy path: diff appears in issue body with marker and section heading
  2. Idempotency: second call for same PR makes no edit
  3. Size cap: 25KB diff truncated with `... (truncated, full diff at PR #N)` note
  4. `origin:interactive` skip: static analysis confirms guard is before carry-forward call
  5. Empty diff: gracefully skipped without issue edit

## Verification

title: GH#19137: fix(dispatch-dedup-cost): broaden token-spend sed pattern for any prefix and time format
body:
## Summary

Addresses review bot feedback from PR #18931: the sed pattern used to normalize token-spend footer strings in `_sum_issue_token_spend` was fragile — it only stripped time infixes for the `spent` prefix and was limited to 1-2 time units (`[0-9]+[dhms]( [0-9]+[mh])?`).

**Change:** Replace the narrow infix-stripping sed pattern with a broader one that:
- Handles both `spent` and `has used` prefixes
- Handles any time format (including days+hours+minutes), using `(.* and )?` to match the optional infix
- Keeps the subsequent `grep -oE '(spent|has used) [0-9,]+ tokens'` extraction intact

**Before:**
```
sed -E 's/(spent )[0-9]+[dhms]( [0-9]+[mh])? and /\1/g'
```

**After:**
```
sed -E 's/(spent|has used) (.* and )?([0-9,]+ tokens)/\1 \3/g'
```

Also updated the inline comment to document the `2d 3h 15m` multi-unit time format example.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-cost.sh` — zero violations
- Logic verified manually against all four documented footer shapes: no-time, minutes, hours+minutes, historical `has used` wording.
